newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy parliament to sit all night on budget vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy parliament to sit all night on budget vote.

text.p: Government parties forced an all-night sitting of Italy's lower house of parliament on Wednesday in response to opposition attempts to talk passage of outstanding 1997 budget measures to a standstill.

The decision to proceed without interruption except for a couple of hours to clean the Chamber of Deputies meant scores of opposition members who had registered to speak would have to make their address in the dead of night.
A vote on the measures was now expected after 0830 GMT on Thursday, Speaker Luciano Violante told the assembly.
Italy's centre-left government resorted to a confidence vote on Tuesday to sweep aside filibustering amendments on the measures submitted by the opposition.
It won that vote with ease but parliamentary rules require a further vote on the item of legislation itself.

Government hopes that the process would be a formality were dashed when 143 deputies said they would exercise a right to speak for up to 10 minutes each before the vote. Most are from the hard-right National Alliance party.

"Your hope of blocking the measures is infantile and it is going to be disappointed," Fabio Mussi, leader in the chamber of the large ex-communist Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), said in a speech proposing the all-night session.
"As you can see, we can use the rules as well," Mussi said before his proposal was accepted on a show of hands.

Italy has adopted a series of increasingly tough budgets over the past five years in a bid to repair the damage done by free-spending administrations at the end of the 1980s and become a founder member of the single European currency.
The latest budget, which was mostly approved by parliament last December, was designed to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($37.5 billion) off the public sector deficit in 1997.
However the final segment, which accounts for 4.3 trillion lire of savings, was only introduced as a cabinet decree. It will become law once exhausted deputies vote on Thursday.
